answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive and cluster-punishable. Each newcomer posts a time-locked bond that only unlocks after many attested epochs. A coordination haven is not enough: peers also compare timing, phrasing, and infrastructure fingerprints. If a cluster looks like one operator spinning wallets around a single oasis of shared keys, the protocol treats that shared cipher of behavior as evidence and slashes every bond in the cluster, so quantity of sockpuppets increases loss instead of influence.
